comparability_notes: Comparable only across runs on the isaac-5.1 official backend at this suite's declared rig: 480x270 RGB, 1.0 m eye height, HFOV 120 deg, 0.05-200 m clip range, 300-step budget. That rig is what this coordinate is measured at going forward, not a replay of the rigs the constituent episode sets were first scored at: the outdoor Gaussian-splat sets ran at 300 steps with a 200 m far plane, the indoor sets at 200 steps with a 100 m far plane. Widening the far plane is a no-op indoors (nothing indoors is beyond 100 m), but the 200-to-300 step change is not calibrated indoors, so a run of this coordinate is not expected to reproduce previously published indoor figures.

One process, one order: the runner renders the mesh scene families (HM3D, MP3D) before the Gaussian-splat ones (InteriorGS, Habitat-GS), and that order is part of the measurement. Loading a Gaussian-splat stage leaves the renderer in a different state that persists for the life of the process -- measured on the reference implementation, reloading one mesh scene repeatedly moves its first frame by at most 1.13/255, inserting another mesh scene by 1.18, and inserting a splat scene by 8.78, after which it stays there; the shift was worth 4-6 success-rate points over 916 indoor episodes. Clearing the stage does not undo it and no renderer setting differs across the boundary, and this CLI cannot restart itself mid-run, so the remedy here is the ordering: no mesh episode is ever rendered after a splat load. The reverse direction -- splat scenes in a process that has loaded mesh scenes -- is not measured, and is the residual difference from an implementation that starts a fresh process at every scene-family boundary.

Success uses the NavNuances LR-towards protocol: the camera ends within the episode's success radius of the object centre with the object inside a 120 deg horizontal field of view. Ending near the object while facing away is not a success.

Scored at 2.0 m indoors and 3.0 m outdoors, selected by the episode's metadata.scene_class. scene.dataset is not the discriminator: the Habitat-GS family holds indoor captures as well as outdoor ones, and reading the radius off the dataset mis-scored 51 episodes of an earlier release.

dataset.notice: Published as insight_bench/v1/episodes.jsonl (1097 JSONL records) in the INSIGHT-Bench dataset release; pass it to the runner with --episodes. Every record carries metadata.scene_class (one of Apartment, House, Commercial, Institution, Outdoor) and metadata.instr_type (one of Base, Direction, Relation, Extremum, Ordinal), and no field of the file holds non-ASCII text. Against the file the retired insight-bench-v1@0.1.0 pinned, the scene_class values are translated from Chinese onto that vocabulary and the instr_type values capitalised onto it, and the Chinese metadata.objnav.zh_vlm provenance string is dropped from the 152 records that carried it, because the English instruction translated from it is already the record's instruction field. Every scoring field is byte-identical to that file. The SHA-256 this coordinate pins is of that published file, and the file you pass is checked against it before a run starts.

description: 1097 object-goal navigation episodes over 210 scenes from four families (HM3D, MP3D, InteriorGS, Habitat-GS), scored with the NavNuances LR-towards protocol on the isaac-5.1 simulator backend at 2.0 m indoors and 3.0 m outdoors. The episode file and the scene assets are supplied by the user: three of the four scene families are licence-gated and this distribution neither ships nor downloads them.
